title: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit — Unit 4

blocks.en: The Spirit in the Old Testament
blocks.es_reference: El Espíritu en el Antiguo Testamento

blocks.en: The Spirit's work before Pentecost: in creation, equipping God's servants, upon judges, kings, and prophets, and the promise of a greater day
blocks.es_reference: La obra del Espíritu antes de Pentecostés: en la creación, equipando a los siervos de Dios, sobre jueces, reyes y profetas, y la promesa de un día mayor

blocks.en: 1. The Spirit Was There from the Beginning
blocks.es_reference: 1. El Espíritu estaba allí desde el principio

blocks.en: When we open the Bible to study the Holy Spirit, we do not have to read far, for He is there in the second verse. Before the first creature ever drew breath, "the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters" (Genesis 1:2). The Spirit is no newcomer who arrives only in the book of Acts; He has been at work since the first page of Scripture. Job confessed, "The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life" (Job 33:4), and the psalmist sang to the Lord, "You send forth Your Spirit, they are created" (Psalm 104:30). The same Spirit who would one day be poured out upon the church was already brooding over the dark waters at the dawn of the world. By that same breath the skies themselves were made, for Job said, "By His Spirit He adorned the heavens" (Job 26:13), and the psalmist wrote, "By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all the host of them by the breath of His mouth" (Psalm 33:6). If we would know Him well, we must follow His work through the whole Old Testament, watching what He does long before Pentecost ever comes.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando abrimos la Biblia para estudiar al Espíritu Santo, no tenemos que leer mucho, pues Él está en el segundo versículo. Antes de que criatura alguna respirara, “el Espíritu de Dios se movía sobre la faz de las aguas” (Génesis 1:2). El Espíritu no es ningún recién llegado que aparece solo en el libro de los Hechos; ha estado obrando desde la primera página de la Escritura. Job confesó: “El Espíritu de Dios me hizo, y el soplo del Omnipotente me dio vida” (Job 33:4), y el salmista cantó al Señor: “Envías tu Espíritu, son creados” (Salmo 104:30). El mismo Espíritu que un día sería derramado sobre la iglesia ya empollaba sobre las aguas oscuras en el amanecer del mundo. Por ese mismo soplo fueron hechos los cielos, pues Job dijo: “Su Espíritu adornó los cielos” (Job 26:13), y el salmista escribió: “Por la palabra de Jehová fueron hechos los cielos, y todo el ejército de ellos por el aliento de su boca” (Salmo 33:6). Si hemos de conocerlo bien, debemos seguir su obra a través de todo el Antiguo Testamento, observando lo que hace mucho antes de que llegue Pentecostés.

blocks.en: 2. The Spirit Who Equips for Service
blocks.es_reference: 2. El Espíritu que capacita para el servicio

blocks.en: One of the first things the Old Testament teaches us about the Spirit is that He gives ability for the work of God. When the tabernacle was to be built, God chose a craftsman named Bezalel and said, "I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship" (Exodus 31:3). The skill to cut a gem and to work fine gold for God's house was itself a gift of the Spirit. Later, when the burden of leading Israel grew too heavy for one man, the Lord "took of the Spirit that was upon him, and placed the same upon the seventy elders" (Numbers 11:25), and they were able to share the load with Moses. From the very beginning the Spirit has been the One who fits ordinary people for service they could never render on their own. Indeed, the great rule of all God's work was given to Zerubbabel in a single sentence: "Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of hosts" (Zechariah 4:6). Whatever is truly done for God is done by the Spirit, and not by the strength of men.
blocks.es_reference: Una de las primeras cosas que el Antiguo Testamento nos enseña acerca del Espíritu es que da capacidad para la obra de Dios. Cuando se iba a construir el tabernáculo, Dios escogió a un artesano llamado Bezaleel y dijo: “Lo he llenado del Espíritu de Dios, en sabiduría y en inteligencia, en ciencia y en todo arte” (Éxodo 31:3). La destreza para tallar una piedra preciosa y labrar oro fino para la casa de Dios era ella misma un don del Espíritu. Más tarde, cuando la carga de guiar a Israel se hizo demasiado pesada para un solo hombre, el Señor “tomó del espíritu que estaba en él, y lo puso en los setenta ancianos” (Números 11:25), y pudieron compartir la carga con Moisés. Desde el principio mismo el Espíritu ha sido Aquel que capacita a personas comunes para un servicio que jamás podrían rendir por sí solas. En verdad, la gran regla de toda la obra de Dios se dio a Zorobabel en una sola frase: “No con ejército, ni con fuerza, sino con mi Espíritu, ha dicho Jehová de los ejércitos” (Zacarías 4:6). Cuanto se hace de veras para Dios se hace por el Espíritu, y no por la fuerza de los hombres.

blocks.en: 3. The Spirit upon the Judges
blocks.es_reference: 3. El Espíritu sobre los jueces

blocks.en: In the days of the judges we watch the Spirit come upon men to deliver God's people. When Israel cried out under oppression, "the Spirit of the LORD came upon" Othniel, and he judged Israel and went out to war and won (Judges 3:10). The same is said of Gideon: "the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon" (Judges 6:34), and a frightened man who had been threshing wheat in hiding became a mighty deliverer. With Samson the words are stronger still, for "the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him" (Judges 14:6), and his great strength was never his own but the Spirit's gift. Notice the pattern that runs through them all: the Spirit came upon a man for a task, equipping him to do what he could never have done alone. So it was with Jephthah too, for "the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah" (Judges 11:29) before he went out to battle. These were not flawless men, as their lives plainly show, yet the Spirit came upon them to accomplish the work God had appointed.
blocks.es_reference: En los días de los jueces vemos al Espíritu venir sobre hombres para librar al pueblo de Dios. Cuando Israel clamó bajo la opresión, “el Espíritu de Jehová vino sobre” Otoniel, y juzgó a Israel y salió a la guerra y venció (Jueces 3:10). Lo mismo se dice de Gedeón: “el Espíritu de Jehová vino sobre Gedeón” (Jueces 6:34), y un hombre atemorizado que trillaba trigo a escondidas llegó a ser un poderoso libertador. Con Sansón las palabras son aún más fuertes, pues “el Espíritu de Jehová vino poderosamente sobre él” (Jueces 14:6), y su gran fuerza nunca fue suya sino don del Espíritu. Note el patrón que corre por todos ellos: el Espíritu venía sobre un hombre para una tarea, capacitándolo para hacer lo que nunca habría podido hacer solo. Así fue también con Jefté, pues “el Espíritu de Jehová vino sobre Jefté” (Jueces 11:29) antes de salir a la batalla. No eran hombres sin falta, como sus vidas claramente muestran, y sin embargo el Espíritu venía sobre ellos para cumplir la obra que Dios había señalado.

blocks.en: 4. The Spirit upon the Kings
blocks.es_reference: 4. El Espíritu sobre los reyes

blocks.en: When Israel asked for a king, the Spirit was given to the king as well. Of Saul it was said, "the Spirit of God came upon him" (1 Samuel 10:10); indeed Samuel had promised that the Spirit would come upon him and turn him "into another man" (1 Samuel 10:6), and for a season he prophesied and led. But Saul's life holds a solemn warning, for after his long rebellion "the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul" (1 Samuel 16:14). What had been given was taken away. When David was anointed in Saul's place, "the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward" (1 Samuel 16:13). David had seen what became of Saul, and so when he himself fell into sin he prayed that trembling prayer, "Do not cast me away from Your presence, and do not take Your Holy Spirit from me" (Psalm 51:11). Here is a man who knew the Spirit's presence and dreaded above all things to lose it.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Israel pidió un rey, el Espíritu fue dado también al rey. De Saúl se dijo: “el Espíritu de Dios vino sobre él” (1 Samuel 10:10); en verdad Samuel había prometido que el Espíritu vendría sobre él y lo mudaría “en otro hombre” (1 Samuel 10:6), y por una temporada profetizó y guió. Pero la vida de Saúl encierra una solemne advertencia, pues tras su larga rebelión “el Espíritu de Jehová se apartó de Saúl” (1 Samuel 16:14). Lo que había sido dado le fue quitado. Cuando David fue ungido en lugar de Saúl, “el Espíritu de Jehová vino sobre David de aquel día en adelante” (1 Samuel 16:13). David había visto lo que fue de Saúl, y por eso, cuando él mismo cayó en pecado, oró aquella temblorosa oración: “No me eches de delante de ti, y no quites de mí tu santo Espíritu” (Salmo 51:11). He aquí un hombre que conoció la presencia del Espíritu y temió sobre todas las cosas perderla.

blocks.en: 5. The Spirit in the Prophets
blocks.es_reference: 5. El Espíritu en los profetas

blocks.en: Above all, the Spirit was the One who spoke through the prophets. When the word of God came to a prophet, it came by the Spirit. Ezekiel testified, "the Spirit entered me when He spoke to me, and set me on my feet" (Ezekiel 2:2). Micah declared, "I am full of power by the Spirit of the LORD, and of justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression" (Micah 3:8). Long afterward Nehemiah looked back over the centuries and confessed that God had warned His people "by Your Spirit in Your prophets" (Nehemiah 9:30), and Isaiah remembered how God had set "His Holy Spirit" among His people in the days of Moses (Isaiah 63:11). So when Peter later wrote that "holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit" (2 Peter 1:21), he was simply summing up the whole long story of the Old Testament. Zechariah said the same of the generations before him, that the Lord had sent His words "by His Spirit through the former prophets" (Zechariah 7:12). Every true word the prophets ever spoke was the Spirit's word through them.
blocks.es_reference: Sobre todo, el Espíritu fue Aquel que habló por medio de los profetas. Cuando la palabra de Dios venía a un profeta, venía por el Espíritu. Ezequiel testificó: “entró el Espíritu en mí cuando me habló, y me afirmó sobre mis pies” (Ezequiel 2:2). Miqueas declaró: “estoy lleno de poder del Espíritu de Jehová, y de juicio y de fuerza, para denunciar a Jacob su rebelión” (Miqueas 3:8). Mucho después, Nehemías miró atrás por los siglos y confesó que Dios había amonestado a su pueblo “por tu Espíritu por mano de tus profetas” (Nehemías 9:30), e Isaías recordó cómo Dios había puesto “su santo Espíritu” en medio de su pueblo en los días de Moisés (Isaías 63:11). Así que cuando Pedro escribió más tarde que “los santos hombres de Dios hablaron siendo inspirados por el Espíritu Santo” (2 Pedro 1:21), no hacía sino resumir toda la larga historia del Antiguo Testamento. Zacarías dijo lo mismo de las generaciones anteriores, que el Señor había enviado sus palabras “por su Espíritu por medio de los primeros profetas” (Zacarías 7:12). Toda palabra verdadera que los profetas jamás hablaron fue la palabra del Espíritu por medio de ellos.

blocks.en: 6. The Measure of the Old Covenant
blocks.es_reference: 6. La medida del antiguo pacto

blocks.en: Now we must notice something common to all these accounts, for it prepares us for what comes next. In the Old Testament the Spirit usually came upon chosen individuals, a craftsman, a judge, a king, a prophet, and He came for a particular task. He was not yet poured out upon all of God's people alike. What is more, His coming could be withdrawn, as Saul learned to his sorrow and as David feared in his prayer. The Spirit was truly at work, and God's faithful people knew Him and loved Him; but His coming in those days was selective, and in some measure it could be taken away. We should not think the Old Testament saints were strangers to the Spirit, for they were not; David and the prophets walked closely with Him. The difference lay in the manner and the measure of His coming. He rested upon some and not others, He came for seasons and tasks, and He could depart. The Old Testament saints walked in the bright light of morning, but a fuller noonday was still to come, and they themselves were taught to lift their eyes and look for it.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora debemos notar algo común a todos estos relatos, pues nos prepara para lo que viene después. En el Antiguo Testamento el Espíritu venía por lo general sobre individuos escogidos, un artesano, un juez, un rey, un profeta, y venía para una tarea particular. Aún no era derramado sobre todo el pueblo de Dios por igual. Más aún, su venida podía ser retirada, como Saúl aprendió para su dolor y como David temió en su oración. El Espíritu obraba de veras, y el pueblo fiel de Dios lo conocía y lo amaba; pero su venida en aquellos días era selectiva, y en alguna medida podía ser quitada. No debemos pensar que los santos del Antiguo Testamento eran extraños al Espíritu, pues no lo eran; David y los profetas anduvieron de cerca con Él. La diferencia estaba en la manera y la medida de su venida. Reposaba sobre unos y no sobre otros, venía por temporadas y para tareas, y podía apartarse. Los santos del Antiguo Testamento andaban en la clara luz de la mañana, pero un mediodía más pleno estaba aún por venir, y ellos mismos fueron enseñados a alzar los ojos y buscarlo.

blocks.en: 7. The Promise of a Greater Day
blocks.es_reference: 7. La promesa de un día mayor

blocks.en: For God did not leave His people without a promise. Through the prophet Joel He pledged a day unlike any they had known: "I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy" (Joel 2:28). Not a chosen few, but all flesh; not the king and the prophet only, but sons and daughters, menservants and maidservants alike. Through Ezekiel God promised an inward work as well: "I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes" (Ezekiel 36:27), and in the valley of dry bones He vowed, "I will put My Spirit in you, and you shall live" (Ezekiel 37:14). Isaiah waited for the same blessing, longing for the day "till the Spirit is poured upon us from on high" (Isaiah 32:15), and he heard God say, "I will pour My Spirit on your descendants" (Isaiah 44:3). What the old covenant gave to a few, the new covenant would give to all; what could once be withdrawn, God now promised to put within His people and not remove. The Old Testament does not close in the Spirit's absence; it closes leaning forward, waiting for the day when the Spirit would be poured out on all and would come to dwell within God's people to stay.
blocks.es_reference: Pues Dios no dejó a su pueblo sin promesa. Por el profeta Joel prometió un día como ninguno que hubieran conocido: “derramaré mi Espíritu sobre toda carne; y profetizarán vuestros hijos y vuestras hijas” (Joel 2:28). No unos pocos escogidos, sino toda carne; no solo el rey y el profeta, sino hijos e hijas, siervos y siervas por igual. Por Ezequiel Dios prometió también una obra interior: “pondré dentro de vosotros mi Espíritu, y haré que andéis en mis estatutos” (Ezequiel 36:27), y en el valle de los huesos secos juró: “pondré mi Espíritu en vosotros, y viviréis” (Ezequiel 37:14). Isaías esperaba la misma bendición, anhelando el día “hasta que sobre nosotros sea derramado el Espíritu de lo alto” (Isaías 32:15), y oyó decir a Dios: “derramaré mi Espíritu sobre tu simiente” (Isaías 44:3). Lo que el antiguo pacto dio a unos pocos, el nuevo pacto lo daría a todos; lo que una vez podía ser retirado, Dios ahora prometía poner dentro de su pueblo y no quitarlo. El Antiguo Testamento no cierra en la ausencia del Espíritu; cierra inclinándose hacia adelante, esperando el día en que el Espíritu sería derramado sobre todos y vendría a morar dentro del pueblo de Dios para quedarse.

blocks.en: 8. The Spirit and the Coming Messiah
blocks.es_reference: 8. El Espíritu y el Mesías que ha de venir

blocks.en: There was one promise greater than all the rest. The Spirit who would be poured out on all flesh would first rest, in His fullness, upon the Coming One. Isaiah foretold of the Messiah, "The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might" (Isaiah 11:2). Of the same chosen Servant God said, "I have put My Spirit upon Him; He will bring forth justice to the Gentiles" (Isaiah 42:1). And the Servant Himself would one day stand and say, "The Spirit of the LORD God is upon Me, because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good tidings to the poor" (Isaiah 61:1). The whole Old Testament, then, points beyond itself. The Spirit who hovered over creation, who equipped the craftsmen, who came upon the judges and kings, who spoke through the prophets, and who was promised to all flesh, would come first and fully upon Christ Himself. To see how that ancient promise was kept, we must turn to the Gospels and to the great day of Pentecost, when the long waiting of the Old Testament would at last be answered.
blocks.es_reference: Había una promesa mayor que todas las demás. El Espíritu que sería derramado sobre toda carne reposaría primero, en su plenitud, sobre Aquel que había de venir. Isaías profetizó del Mesías: “reposará sobre él el Espíritu de Jehová; espíritu de sabiduría y de inteligencia, espíritu de consejo y de poder” (Isaías 11:2). Del mismo Siervo escogido dijo Dios: “he puesto sobre él mi Espíritu; él traerá justicia a las naciones” (Isaías 42:1). Y el Siervo mismo un día se pondría de pie y diría: “El Espíritu del Señor Jehová está sobre mí, porque me ungió Jehová; me ha enviado a predicar buenas nuevas a los abatidos” (Isaías 61:1). Todo el Antiguo Testamento, pues, señala más allá de sí mismo. El Espíritu que se movía sobre la creación, que equipó a los artesanos, que vino sobre los jueces y los reyes, que habló por los profetas, y que fue prometido a toda carne, vendría primero y plenamente sobre Cristo mismo. Para ver cómo se cumplió aquella antigua promesa, debemos volvernos a los Evangelios y al gran día de Pentecostés, cuando la larga espera del Antiguo Testamento sería al fin respondida.

sa.prompt: Show from the Old Testament that the Spirit was at work in creation, naming at least one text.
sa.model: In the very second verse the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters at creation, in Genesis 1:2. Job said the Spirit of God made him and gives life, and the psalmist said that when God sends forth His Spirit, things are created. The Spirit was at work from the beginning.

sa.prompt: How did the Spirit equip people for service in the Old Testament? Give examples.
sa.model: The Spirit gave ability for God's work. He filled Bezalel with skill to build the tabernacle, and He placed the Spirit that was on Moses upon the seventy elders to share the burden. As Zechariah said, God's work is done not by might nor power but by His Spirit.

sa.prompt: Describe the Spirit's work upon the judges, with an example.
sa.model: In the days of the judges the Spirit came upon men to deliver Israel from oppression. The Spirit came upon Gideon, and a frightened man became a deliverer; and the Spirit came mightily upon Samson, so his great strength was the Spirit's gift, not his own. The Spirit empowered them for the task.

sa.prompt: What does the life of Saul, together with David's prayer, teach about the Spirit's coming in the Old Testament?
sa.model: It teaches that the Spirit came upon a person but could also be withdrawn. After Saul rebelled, the Spirit of the LORD departed from him; and David, who had seen this, prayed that God would not take His Holy Spirit from him. The Spirit's presence in those days could be lost.

sa.prompt: How was the Holy Spirit at work in the Old Testament prophets?
sa.model: The Spirit was the One who spoke through the prophets; when the word of God came to a prophet, it came by the Spirit. Ezekiel said the Spirit entered him, and Micah was full of power by the Spirit. As Peter wrote, holy men spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.

sa.prompt: What was distinctive about the measure of the Spirit under the old covenant?
sa.model: Under the old covenant the Spirit came upon select individuals, a craftsman, a judge, a king, a prophet, and He came for a particular task. He was not yet poured out on all God's people, and His coming could be withdrawn, as with Saul. The manner and measure were selective.

sa.prompt: What did Joel promise about the Spirit, and how was it different from the Old Testament pattern?
sa.model: Joel promised that God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh, so that sons and daughters, menservants and maidservants alike would prophesy. This was different because the Spirit would no longer come upon only a chosen few, but be poured out on all God's people.

sa.prompt: What inward work did Ezekiel promise the Spirit would do?
sa.model: Ezekiel promised that God would put His Spirit within His people and cause them to walk in His statutes, an inward work, not merely a coming upon them from outside. In the valley of dry bones God promised to put His Spirit in them so that they would live.

sa.prompt: What did the Old Testament promise about the Spirit and the Messiah?
sa.model: It promised that the Spirit would rest in His fullness upon the coming Messiah. Isaiah said the Spirit of the LORD would rest upon Him, the Spirit of wisdom and might; God said He had put His Spirit upon His Servant; and the Servant would say the Spirit of the LORD was upon Him to preach good news.

sa.prompt: Briefly summarize the Old Testament story of the Spirit and where it points.
sa.model: The Spirit was at work in creation, equipped craftsmen and leaders, came upon the judges and kings, and spoke through the prophets, always coming upon a few for a task. God then promised to pour Him out on all flesh and put Him within His people. The whole story points to the Spirit coming first upon Christ, and to Pentecost.
